questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A car moving with a speed of $54$ km/h takes a turn of radius $20$ m. A simple pendulum is suspended from the ceiling of the car. Determine the angle made by the string of the pendulum with the vertical during the turning. (Take $g=10$ m/s$^2$)
questions.solution:
Speed of the car, $v = 54 \times \dfrac{5}{18} = 15$ m/s.

In the frame of the car, the pendulum bob experiences a pseudo force (centrifugal force) horizontally outwards and the gravitational force downwards.

Let $T$ be the tension in the string and $\theta$ be the angle it makes with the vertical. For equilibrium in the car's frame, the horizontal and vertical forces balance:

$T \sin \theta = \dfrac{mv^2}{r}$

$T \cos \theta = mg$

Dividing the two equations, we get:

$\tan \theta = \dfrac{v^2}{rg}$

Substituting the given values $v = 15$ m/s, $r = 20$ m, and $g = 10$ m/s$^2$:

$\tan \theta = \dfrac{(15)^2}{20 \times 10} = \dfrac{225}{200} = 1.125$

$\theta = \tan^{-1}(1.125)$

Answer: $\tan^{-1}(1.125)$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two identical bodies, projected with the same speed at two different angles cover the same horizontal range $R$. If the time of flight of these bodies are $5$ s and $10$ s, respectively, then the value of $R$ is ________ m. (Take $g=10$ m/s$^2$)
questions.solution:
For two projectiles to have the same horizontal range $R$ with the same initial speed $u$, their angles of projection must be complementary, i.e., $\theta$ and $90^\circ - \theta$.

The times of flight for these two angles are given by:
$t_1 = \dfrac{2u \sin \theta}{g}$
$t_2 = \dfrac{2u \cos \theta}{g}$

Multiplying $t_1$ and $t_2$, we get:
$t_1 t_2 = \left(\dfrac{2u \sin \theta}{g}\right) \left(\dfrac{2u \cos \theta}{g}\right) = \dfrac{2}{g} \left(\dfrac{u^2 (2 \sin \theta \cos \theta)}{g}\right)$

Since the horizontal range is $R = \dfrac{u^2 \sin 2\theta}{g}$, we can write:
$t_1 t_2 = \dfrac{2R}{g}$

Given $t_1 = 5$ s, $t_2 = 10$ s, and $g = 10$ m/s$^2$, substituting these values:
$5 \times 10 = \dfrac{2R}{10}$

$50 = \dfrac{2R}{10}$

$2R = 500 \Rightarrow R = 250$ m

Answer: $250$

questions.q: If $x$ and $y$ coordinates of a projectile as a function of time $(t)$ are given as $24t$ and $43.6t-4.9t^2$, respectively, then the angle (in degrees) made by the projectile with horizontal when $t=2$ s is ______.
questions.solution:
The velocity components of the projectile are given by the derivatives of the position coordinates with respect to time.

$v_x = \dfrac{dx}{dt} = \dfrac{d}{dt}(24t) = 24$

$v_y = \dfrac{dy}{dt} = \dfrac{d}{dt}(43.6t - 4.9t^2) = 43.6 - 9.8t$

At $t = 2$ s, the velocity components are:

$v_x = 24$

$v_y = 43.6 - 9.8(2) = 43.6 - 19.6 = 24$

The angle $\theta$ made by the velocity vector with the horizontal is given by:

$\tan \theta = \dfrac{v_y}{v_x} = \dfrac{24}{24} = 1$

$\theta = 45^{\circ}$

Answer: $45$

questions.q: Two projectiles are projected with the same initial velocities at the $15^\circ$ and $30^\circ$ with respect to the horizontal. The ratio of their ranges is $1:x$. The value of $x$ is:
questions.solution:
The horizontal range of a projectile is given by the formula $R = \dfrac{u^2 \sin(2\theta)}{g}$.

For the first projectile, the angle of projection is $\theta_1 = 15^\circ$.

$R_1 = \dfrac{u^2 \sin(2 \times 15^\circ)}{g} = \dfrac{u^2 \sin(30^\circ)}{g} = \dfrac{u^2}{2g}$

For the second projectile, the angle of projection is $\theta_2 = 30^\circ$.

$R_2 = \dfrac{u^2 \sin(2 \times 30^\circ)}{g} = \dfrac{u^2 \sin(60^\circ)}{g} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}u^2}{2g}$

The ratio of their ranges is:

$\dfrac{R_1}{R_2} = \dfrac{\dfrac{u^2}{2g}}{\dfrac{\sqrt{3}u^2}{2g}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$

Given that the ratio is $1:x$, we get $x = \sqrt{3}$.

Answer: $\sqrt{3}$

questions.q:
A boy throws a ball into air at $45^{\circ}$ from the horizontal to land it on a roof of a building of height $H$. If the ball attains maximum height in 2 s and lands on the building in 3 s after launch, then value of $H$ is $\_\_\_\_$ m.
$\left(\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^{2}\right)$
questions.solution:
For projectile motion at 45°, vertical component of initial velocity:
$v_{0y} = v_0 \sin 45° = \frac{v_0}{\sqrt{2}}$
Maximum height occurs at $t = 2$ s when $v_y = 0$:
$0 = v_{0y} - gt$
$\Rightarrow v_{0y} = 10 \times 2 = 20$ m/s
Thus $\frac{v_0}{\sqrt{2}} = 20$, so $v_0 = 20\sqrt{2}$ m/s
Height at landing time $t = 3$ s:
$H = v_{0y}t - \frac{1}{2}gt^2 = 20 \times 3 - \frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 9$
$= 60 - 45 = 15$ m

questions.q: An object is projected with kinetic energy $K$ from a point $A$ at an angle $60^{\circ}$ with the horizontal. The ratio of the difference in kinetic energies at points $B$ and $C$ to that at point $A$ (see figure), in the absence of air friction is :
questions.solution:
At A: $KE_A = K$, $v_A = v$, angle $= 60°$.
At B (highest point): $v_B = v\cos 60° = v/2$, so $KE_B = K/4$.
At C (same level as A): by energy conservation, $KE_C = K$.
$|KE_B - KE_C| = |K/4 - K| = 3K/4$.
Ratio $= \frac{3K/4}{K} = \frac{3}{4}$, i.e., $3:4$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A river of width 200 m is flowing from west to east with a speed of $18 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{h}$. A boat, moving with speed of $36 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{h}$ in still water, is made to travel one-round trip (bank to bank of the river). Minimum time taken by the boat for this journey and also the displacement along the river bank are $\_\_\_\_$ and $\_\_\_\_$ respectively.
questions.solution:
Width of the river $d = 200$ m.
Speed of river $v_r = 18$ km/h $= 18 \times \frac{5}{18} = 5$ m/s.
Speed of boat in still water $v_b = 36$ km/h $= 36 \times \frac{5}{18} = 10$ m/s.
For minimum time to cross the river, the boat must head perpendicular to the river flow (at $90^\circ$ to the bank).
Time taken to cross once $t = \frac{d}{v_b} = \frac{200}{10} = 20$ s.
For a round trip (bank to bank and back), the total minimum time is $T = 2t = 2 \times 20 = 40$ s.
During the first crossing, the drift (displacement along the bank) is $x_1 = v_r \times t = 5 \times 20 = 100$ m.
During the return trip, to minimize time, the boat again heads perpendicular to the flow relative to the water. The river continues to flow in the same direction, so the drift is again in the same direction as the first trip.
Return drift $x_2 = v_r \times t = 5 \times 20 = 100$ m.
Total displacement along the river bank $= x_1 + x_2 = 100 + 100 = 200$ m.
Thus, minimum time is $40$ s and displacement is $200$ m.

questions.q: A body starts falling freely from height $H$ hits an inclined plane in its path at height $h$. As a result of this perfectly elastic impact, the direction of the velocity of the body becomes horizontal. The value of $\dfrac{H}{h}$ for which the body will take the maximum time to reach the ground is _____.
questions.solution:
Total time of flight $= T$ can be written as, 

$T = \sqrt{\dfrac{2h}{g}} + \sqrt{\dfrac{2\left(H - h\right)}{g}}$

For maximum time $= \dfrac{dT}{dh} = 0$

$⇒ \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{g}}\left(\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{h}} - \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{H - h}}\right) = 0$

$⇒ \sqrt{H - h} = \sqrt{h}$

$⇒ h = \dfrac{H}{2} ⇒ \dfrac{H}{h} = 2$

questions.solution:
Let the frame of reference to be attached to the car with x-axis along horizontal direction and y-axis along vertical direction. Since the frame of reference is a rotating frame, a centrifugal force term should be added while applying Newton's second law.

Let $\theta$ be the angle made by the pendulum with the vertical.

Applying Newton's second law for horizontal direction:

$Tsin\theta - \dfrac{m{v}^{2}}{R} = 0$ (since the acceleration of the pendulum in the rotating frame is 0).

$∴ Tsin\theta = \dfrac{m{v}^{2}}{R}$ ..........(1)

Applying Newton's second law for vertical direction:

$Tcos\theta - mg = 0$

$⇒ Tcos\theta = mg$ ..........(2)

Dividing equation 1 by equation 2:

$tan\theta = \dfrac{{v}^{2}}{Rg} = \dfrac{{\left(20\right)}^{2}}{\left(40\right)\left(10\right)} = 1 ⇒ \theta = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$

questions.solution:
It is given that the projectile passes through $\left(20, 10\right)$ and angle of projection is $\theta = 45 °$. Using the trajectory equation,

$y = xtan\theta - \dfrac{g{x}^{2}}{2{u}^{2}\cos^{2}\theta}$

$⇒ 10 = 20 - \dfrac{\left(10\right)\left(100\right)}{{u}^{2}}$

$T = \dfrac{2usin\theta}{g}$

$⇒ T = \dfrac{\left(2\right)\left(20\right)}{\sqrt{2}\left(10\right)} = 2\sqrt{2}s ⇒ \dfrac{T}{\sqrt{2}} = 2s$

Now velocity of the projectile at any time $t$ can be written as,

$\overset{\to}{v} = ucos\theta\overset{^}{i} + \left(usin\theta - gt\right)\overset{^}{j}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{v} = 10\sqrt{2}\overset{^}{i} + ( 10\sqrt{2} - 10\left(2\right) ] \overset{^}{j}m{s}^{- 1}$

Therefore, momentum $\overset{\to}{p} = M\overset{\to}{v} = 100\sqrt{2}\overset{^}{i} + \left(100\sqrt{2} - 200\right)\overset{^}{j}Ns$

questions.q: A small bob tied at one end of a thin string of length $1m$ is describing a vertical circle so that the maximum and minimum tension in the string is in the ratio $5: 1$. The velocity of the bob at the highest position is ______ $m{s}^{- 1}$. (Take $g = 10m{s}^{- 2}$)
questions.solution:
Let the speed of bob at lowest position be ${v}_{1}$ and at the highest position be ${v}_{2}$.

Maximum tension is at lowest position and minimum tension is at the highest position.
Now, using, conservation of mechanical energy,

$\dfrac{1}{2}m{v}_{1}^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}_{2}^{2} + mg2l$

$⇒ {v}_{1}^{2} = {v}_{2}^{2} + 4gl . . . . \left(1\right)$

Now, ${T}_{max} - mg = \dfrac{m{v}_{1}^{2}}{l}$

$⇒ {T}_{max} = mg + \dfrac{m{v}_{1}^{2}}{l}$

$\text{ and } {T}_{min} + mg = \dfrac{m{v}_{2}^{2}}{l}$

$⇒ {T}_{min} = \dfrac{m{v}_{2}^{2}}{l} - mg$

$\dfrac{{T}_{max}}{{T}_{min}} = \dfrac{5}{1}$

$⇒ \dfrac{mg + \dfrac{m{v}_{1}^{2}}{l}}{\dfrac{m{v}_{2}^{2}}{l} - mg} = \dfrac{5}{1}$

$⇒ mg + \dfrac{m{v}_{1}^{2}}{l} = \left[\dfrac{m{v}_{2}^{2}}{l} - mg\right]5$

$⇒ mg + \dfrac{m}{l}\left[{v}_{2}^{2} + 4gl\right] = \dfrac{5m{v}_{2}^{2}}{l} - 5mg$

$⇒ mg + \dfrac{m{v}_{2}^{2}}{l} + 4mg = \dfrac{5m{v}_{2}^{2}}{l} - 5mg$

$⇒ 10mg = \dfrac{4m{v}_{2}^{2}}{l}$

${v}_{2} = \dfrac{10 \times 10 \times 1}{4}$

Thus, the velocity of the bob at the highest position is $5m{s}^{- 1} .$

questions.q: In a car race on straight road, car $A$ takes a time $t$ less than car $B$ at the finish and passes finishing point with a speed $v$ more than that of car $B .$ Both the cars start from rest and travel with constant acceleration ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}$ respectively. Then $v$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given,
Initially both car is at rest, so ${u}_{1} = {u}_{2} = 0$
Acceleration of car $A \text{ and } B$ is ${a}_{1} \text{ and } {a}_{2}$

Let us assume,
Time of reach to destination of car $A$ is, ${t}_{1} = {t}_{0}$
Time of reach to destination of car $B$ is, ${t}_{2} = {t}_{0} + t$

Using second equation of motion, we have
${u}_{1}t + \dfrac{1}{2}{a}_{1}{t}_{1}^{2} = {u}_{2}t + \dfrac{1}{2}{a}_{2}{{t}_{2}}^{2}$
$⇒ 0 \times t + \dfrac{1}{2}{a}_{1}{t}_{0}^{2} = 0 \times t + \dfrac{1}{2}{a}_{2}{\left({t}_{0} + t\right)}^{2}$
$⇒ \sqrt{\dfrac{{a}_{1}}{{a}_{2}}}{t}_{0} = {t}_{0} + t$
$⇒ {t}_{0} = \dfrac{t}{\sqrt{\dfrac{{a}_{1}}{{a}_{2}}} - 1}$

From first equation of motion, we have
$\begin{cases}{v}_{1} = {a}_{1}{t}_{0} \text{ and } & {v}_{2} = {a}_{2}\left({t}_{0} + t\right)\end{cases}$
$⇒ v = {v}_{1} - {v}_{2} = \left({a}_{1} - {a}_{2}\right){t}_{0} - {a}_{2}t$
$⇒ v = \left({a}_{1} - {a}_{2}\right)\dfrac{t}{\sqrt{\dfrac{{a}_{1}}{{a}_{2}}} - 1} - {a}_{2}t$
$⇒ v = t\left(\dfrac{{a}_{1}\sqrt{{a}_{2}}}{{\sqrt{a}}_{1} - {\sqrt{a}}_{2}} - \dfrac{{a}_{2}{\sqrt{a}}_{2}}{{\sqrt{a}}_{1} - {\sqrt{a}}_{2}} - {a}_{2}\right)$
$⇒ v = t\left(\dfrac{{a}_{1}\sqrt{{a}_{2}} - {a}_{2}{\sqrt{a}}_{1}}{{\sqrt{a}}_{1} - {\sqrt{a}}_{2}}\right)$
$⇒ v = \sqrt{{a}_{1} . {a}_{2}}t$
